## 2026-09-20 — OPC UA semantic-model migration and validation

Discovery used three materially different modes: analog searches from the current OPC UA leaders and migration queue; code/file-oriented searches around NodeSet validators, model compilers and companion-model tooling; and obscure/older modeler discovery. Three new industrial candidates were materially inspected.

### cesmii/CESMII-NodeSet-Utilities — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 28/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/cesmii/CESMII-NodeSet-Utilities
- Exact revision: `f7a5a727909a1abf8a98692678fcce0f340a0750`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Apache-2.0 OPC UA semantic-model toolchain with Cloud Library dependency resolution, NodeSet import/model persistence and a dedicated NodeSetValidator. The inspected source tree includes `CESMII.OpcUa.CloudLibraryResolver`, `CESMII.OpcUa.NodeSetImporter`, EF/model-factory projects and `CESMII.OpcUa.NodeSetValidator`; the validator includes a roughly 43 KB `TheValidator.cs`, UA-server state handling and a CLI/config path that can connect to an OPC UA server, resolve NodeSets/dependencies from a Cloud Library endpoint/local cache and emit validation events with severity.
- Rare / undernoticed value: The existing portfolio is already rich in wire-protocol stacks; this closes the harder semantic-drift gap. Companion-model, namespace, dependency and type changes can break a migration even when sessions/read-write/subscriptions still work.
- Buyer/problem: Industrial OEMs, SCADA/MES vendors, companion-spec implementers and integrators upgrading firmware/SDKs or migrating servers where NodeSet/model drift can silently invalidate client assumptions.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Fixed-price OPC UA semantic migration gate: ingest customer-authorized current/target NodeSets and a target server, resolve dependencies, validate the exposed model, diff namespace/type/reference changes and hand the resulting risky nodes to the existing S2OPC/open62541/node-opcua runtime regression pack.
- Build-time/data advantage: Plausibly 2–6+ months of NodeSet dependency/import/model-validation infrastructure and companion-model edge-case discovery compressed.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision/commit; README; Apache-2.0 root license; source-module listing; `CESMII.OpcUa.NodeSetValidator` directory including `TheValidator.cs` and `UAServerStates.cs`; validator README showing server endpoint, Cloud Library endpoint, local NodeSet cache and severity-bearing validation output.
- Actual public license/rights: Apache-2.0 for repository code. OPC Foundation NodeSets/companion specifications, Cloud Library content/service terms, certification marks and customer models remain separate rights surfaces.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code/content is treated as separately commercially authorized for prioritization; that does not extend to independently owned NodeSets, standards, trademarks, patents, Cloud Library content or customer data.
- Reuse classification: Strong reusable semantic-validation layer with per-model/source rights diligence.
- Score: A4 speed / B4 ceiling / C5 compression / D5 rarity / E5 evidence / F5 rights clarity = **28/30**.
- Combination opportunities: `CESMII NodeSet Utilities + OPCFoundation/UA-ModelCompiler + UA-.NETStandard MigrationAnalyzer + S2OPC/open62541/node-opcua` creates a much stronger OPC UA migration product: compile/normalize the model -> validate semantic dependencies/drift -> migrate the .NET application where relevant -> falsify live behavior across independent stacks.
- Next action: Build a fixture with two revisions of one public/customer-authorized companion model containing namespace/type/reference changes, validate both against controlled servers, and produce a machine-readable semantic-diff plus runtime-regression report.

### OPCFoundation/UA-ModelCompiler — STRONG — 27/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/OPCFoundation/UA-ModelCompiler
- Exact revision: `1a17d31a909e4c2c7e977d983b2920508c024bf7`

- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Current OPC Foundation model compiler for turning OPC UA model-design inputs into NodeSet2 and generated SDK artifacts, and for reverse/model conversion workflows. The README documents generation paths for C#, C, C++, ANSI C/open62541-oriented output, documentation/CSV/BSD/attribute artifacts and NodeSet compilation/reconstruction.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It supplies the deterministic build/translation step missing between static companion-model assets and the existing runtime protocol stacks. That makes model-version migration reproducible rather than a manual XML/code-generation exercise.
- Buyer/problem: OPC UA server/device OEMs and integrators changing companion models or SDK generations where namespace/type/schema changes must be propagated into generated code and validated without hand-editing large NodeSets.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Customer NodeSet/companion-model upgrade service: compile old and new model inputs, regenerate target-language artifacts, identify namespace/type/reference deltas with CESMII validation, then run live interoperability tests against independent OPC UA peers.
- Build-time/data advantage: Saves months of model compiler/code-generator/reverse-conversion engineering and reduces brittle one-off model migrations.
- Evidence inspected: Exact current revision; README feature/output matrix; root project/build assets including `CompileNodeSets.bat`, standard-type/engineering-unit build paths and model compiler source/project structure. A root `LICENSE` path was not present at this revision; the project README states distribution under the MIT license and references separately licensed OPC redistributables/third-party packages.
- Actual public license/rights: Project README states MIT for repository software; exact per-file/package notices should govern where present. OPC redistributables, NodeSets, companion specifications and third-party packages/assets retain separate rights.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code/content is assumed commercially authorized for prioritization; no implied grant covers OPC Foundation standards/certification marks, third-party NodeSets or customer models.
- Reuse classification: High-value build/migration component; preserve per-file and third-party provenance.
- Score: A4 / B4 / C5 / D4 / E5 / F5 = **27/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Compiler output becomes the normalized input to CESMII validation and the existing S2OPC/open62541/node-opcua cross-stack acceptance matrix. It also strengthens the existing `UA-.NETStandard` migration service by separating source/API migration from information-model migration.
- Next action: Compile and reverse one small two-version NodeSet fixture, compare generated namespace/type mappings, then prove the resulting server models against CESMII validator and two independent OPC UA clients.

## 2026-09-20 — PON/OMCI evidence and optical-service acceptance

Discovery used three materially different modes: analog searches from the FreeACS/Oktopus and network-controller leaders; code/protocol searches around OMCI MIB Upload/service objects and optical path/QoT behavior; and obscure low-attention OMCI analyzers/parsers. Five new telecom candidates were materially inspected.

### RainbowCloudLabs/omcipcap — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 29/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/RainbowCloudLabs/omcipcap
- Exact revision: `80b403cc9fd25bb8161d56b078bff8e08b853d37`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: MIT vendor-neutral OMCI PCAP semantic-analysis toolkit that turns customer-authorized packet captures into structured evidence. The README documents RTT and transaction-ID checks, managed-entity failure reporting, inferred MIB snapshots, semantic `mibdb-diff`, VLAN table interpretation, TCONT -> GEM -> Priority Queue hierarchy reconstruction, topology visualization, JSON/Markdown output and custom vendor-specific ME schema hooks.
- Rare / undernoticed value: This is the evidence plane the emerging PON lab was missing. Instead of merely saying an ONU/OLT flow failed, it can compare golden-vs-target traces and expose which MIB/VLAN/GEM/TCONT/topology semantics changed.
- Buyer/problem: FTTH operators, OLT/ONU vendors and integration labs where OMCI interoperability failures appear late during firmware, OLT-controller or ONU-profile migration and are expensive to root-cause from raw captures.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Fixed-price OMCI migration/regression diagnostic: collect only customer-authorized captures from current and target stacks, run timing/failure/MIB/topology analysis, and deliver a semantic difference packet plus reproducible regression cases before rollout.
- Build-time/data advantage: Plausibly 3–6+ months of OMCI decode, MIB reconstruction, topology/VLAN hierarchy analysis and machine-readable report engineering compressed.
- Evidence inspected: Exact 2026-09-14 revision; MIT license; README feature/CLI matrix; test/examples/utils structure. Important limits were retained: inferred state is only as complete as captured traffic, service switch-over analysis is not yet implemented, and ONU delete/MIB reset reconstruction is incomplete. No live or potentially sensitive capture was accessed.
- Actual public license/rights: MIT for repository code. ITU-T G.988/OMCI specifications, certification/trademarks and customer/operator packet captures remain separate rights/data surfaces.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is assumed commercially authorized for prioritization; the standing permission does not extend to ITU/BBF standards, third-party vendor schemas, trademarks/patents or customer captures.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable evidence tooling under MIT, using only lawful public or customer-authorized captures.
- Score: A5 speed / B5 ceiling / C5 compression / D5 rarity / E4 evidence / F5 rights clarity = **29/30**.
- Combination opportunities: `omcipcap + BroadbandForum/obbaa-vomci + BBSim/VOLTHA/OpenONU-family fixtures` creates a sellable PON migration-evidence loop: drive known service state, capture the wire behavior, and compare semantic MIB/VLAN/TCONT/GEM/topology outcomes. Because OBBAA/OpenCORD components share ecosystem lineage, do not count family agreement as independent conformance proof.
- Next action: Create a sanitized synthetic capture pair for MIB upload + UNI/TCONT/GEM/VLAN provisioning with one deliberate semantic difference; verify that `mibdb-diff` and topology/VLAN outputs isolate it, then add a non-OpenCORD/OBBAA endpoint in a future pass.

### BroadbandForum/obbaa-vomci — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 28/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/BroadbandForum/obbaa-vomci
- Exact revision: `a684434483942cca020446fce411959925e04c13`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Apache-2.0 OB-BAA virtual-OMCI implementation with actual ONU management/service machinery. Deep source inspection verified MIB upload orchestration that sends MIB_UPLOAD then repeated MIB_UPLOAD_NEXT, clears/rebuilds the ONU MIB view and merges returned managed entities. The tree also carries handlers/actions around ONU activation, UNI, TCONT, GEM, VLAN, multicast, MIB/software operations; a concrete `test_uni_tcont_gem.py` sequence performs activation -> UNI configuration -> TCONT creation -> GEM port creation with allocation/GEM IDs, direction and encryption settings.
- Rare / undernoticed value: This is substantially closer to a complete PON service-management workflow than a codec library. MIB synchronization plus service-object lifecycle is exactly the expensive controller/ONU integration work that operators normally validate against scarce OLT/ONT labs.
- Buyer/problem: FTTH operators, access-network integrators and ONU/OLT/controller vendors migrating service profiles, disaggregating OLT management or validating vOMCI behavior before production.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: PON/ONU migration rehearsal: reproduce MIB sync and a minimal broadband service chain in a controlled lab, capture every OMCI step, and return a per-ONU profile compatibility/rollback report before OLT/controller change.
- Build-time/data advantage: Saves many months of OMCI MIB/service-lifecycle/controller integration and gives explicit testable TCONT/GEM/UNI behavior rather than requiring a new vOMCI layer from scratch.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision; Apache-2.0 root license; README/tree; deep `omh_nbi/handlers/onu_mib_upload.py` source; `bin/test_uni_tcont_gem.py`; encode/decode/action family including MIB upload-next paths.
- Actual public license/rights: Apache-2.0 for repository code. BBF/ITU standards, OMCI technology/certification/trademarks/patents, vendor ONU/OLT models and customer profiles remain separate.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is assumed commercially authorized for prioritization; external standards/IPR/vendor/customer rights are not implied.
- Reuse classification: High-value PON management component; preserve standards/vendor/customer boundaries and do not treat same-family implementations as independent oracles.
- Score: A4 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E4 / F5 = **28/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Use OBBAA vOMCI as the stateful service driver and OMCIPcap as the independent evidence/semantic-diff layer. This complements the existing CWMP->USP migration product by validating the access/PON layer underneath the managed CPE.
- Next action: Automate MIB upload + UNI/TCONT/GEM/VLAN lifecycle against a synthetic/customer-authorized ONU fixture, capture the exchanges, and feed them through OMCIPcap. Hunt a non-OBBAA/OpenCORD implementation next so differential claims are not ecosystem-self-referential.

### Telecominfraproject/oopt-gnpy — STRONG — 28/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/Telecominfraproject/oopt-gnpy
- Exact revision: `fd32bf544310ac76172224bf2c2054a7d4e6d87a`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Active BSD-3-Clause optical-network planning/QoT engine that computes optical path feasibility and physical impairments from topology/equipment data and supports path requests/network design workflows. The inspected test tree is broad and fixture-heavy, including amplifier, autodesign/automatic mode, CLI, disjunction, equalization and path/propagation-related cases rather than a single demo.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It adds an independent physical-layer feasibility oracle beneath network/service orchestration. Controller tests can prove RPC/state transitions yet still choose a path that is physically marginal; GNPy lets a migration service test both service intent and optical feasibility.
- Buyer/problem: Carriers, optical-system vendors and transport-network integrators changing OpenROADM/controller/service-planning stacks where wrong path/QoT assumptions can cause failed turn-ups, reroutes or restoration plans.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Fixed-price optical service migration preflight: ingest customer-authorized topology/equipment/request data, compute independent feasibility/QoT, then replay the same service create/reroute/restoration intent through the target controller and deliver path/config/QoT disagreement evidence.
- Build-time/data advantage: Saves many months of optical impairment, equipment-model, route/path-request and validation logic and provides an independent calculation layer rather than trusting the controller's own PCE.
- Evidence inspected: Exact 2026-09-18 revision; README architecture/use cases; BSD-3-Clause license; extensive `tests/` directory with large fixture/data sets and tests for amplifier, equalization, automatic design/mode, disjunction, CLI and related path/network behavior.
- Actual public license/rights: BSD-3-Clause for repository code. Vendor equipment parameters, OpenROADM models/specifications, patents/trademarks and customer topology data remain separate rights/data surfaces.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is assumed commercially authorized for prioritization; external standards/vendor/customer data rights are not implied.
- Reuse classification: Strong independent optical calculation component for an acceptance service.
- Score: A4 / B5 / C5 / D4 / E5 / F5 = **28/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Pair GNPy with the existing Clixon/KNE/Ondatra management-plane stack and refer to the integrator for combination with any retained OpenROADM/TransportPCE-style controller: physical feasibility/QoT becomes an independent gate before service provisioning, reroute and restoration acceptance.
- Next action: Build one small open/customer-authorized optical topology with two candidate paths, deliberately make one marginal, and verify that the controller path decision plus GNPy QoT result can be normalized into one migration-readiness report.

- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is assumed commercially authorized; external OMCI specifications/vendor data are separate.
